description: Fig. 5 is a composite, multiscale characterization figure (declared "Multiscale characterization of nanoparticles", all images from the 1.3Al steel) mixing APT atom maps, HRTEM images with FFT insets, and proximity histograms. (a) APT 3D reconstruction, needle-shaped, with brown 5 at.% C isoconcentration surfaces resolving elongated needle-like ε-carbides arranged in rows; printed scale bar 20 nm. (d) matching APT reconstruction with green 10 at.% Ni+Al isoconcentration surfaces showing a very high density of small near-spherical NiAl clusters; a colour key at bottom left reads green = NiAl, brown = ε-carbide. (b) HRTEM (2 nm scale bar) with a cyan box over an ε-carbide; the FFT inset is labelled (020)Ni, (002)ε, Z=[100]Ni, Z=[110]ε, and the matrix is labelled Bcc. (e) HRTEM (2 nm scale bar) with a green box over B2-NiAl; the FFT inset is labelled (200)Ni, (100)NiAl, Z=[001]. (c) proximity histogram, Composition/at.% (0–20) versus Distance/nm (−5 to ~1.5), arrows Matrix ← and ε-carbide →; C rises from ~1.5 to ~8.5–9 at.% while Ni (~5.5 at.%), Si and Al remain nearly flat. (f) proximity histogram, arrows Matrix ← and Clusters (NiAl) →; Ni and Al rise to ~9 and ~8 at.%, Si, Mo and Cr also enrich, and C falls to ~0. Together the panels show that C-rich hcp ε-carbides and near-spherical B2 NiAl clusters coexist independently with distinct chemical signatures.

subfigures.description: APT 3D atom-map reconstruction (needle/conical shape) of the 1.3Al steel with brown 5 at.% C isoconcentration surfaces, revealing elongated needle-like ε-carbide platelets aligned in rows; printed scale bar 20 nm.

HRTEM image with a 2 nm scale bar; a cyan rectangle marks a region labelled 'ε-carbide' inside a matrix labelled 'Bcc'. Inset FFT with reflections labelled (020)Ni and (002)ε and zone axes Z=[100]Ni and Z=[110]ε.

Proximity histogram: Composition/at.% (0–20) vs Distance/nm (−5 to ~1.5), eight-element legend (C, Ni, Al, V, Si, Mn, Cr, Mo), arrows marking Matrix (left) and ε-carbide (right). C rises steeply from ~1.5 to ~8.5–9 at.% in the carbide; Ni stays ~5.5 at.%, Si ~4 at.%, Al ~2.5–4 at.%; curves carry error bars.

APT reconstruction of the same specimen with green 10 at.% Ni+Al isoconcentration surfaces, showing a very dense dispersion of small near-spherical NiAl clusters. Colour key below: green square = NiAl, brown = ε-carbide.
HRTEM image with a 2 nm scale bar; a green rectangle encloses a region labelled 'B2-NiAl' within the 'Bcc' matrix. Inset FFT labelled (200)Ni and (100)NiAl with Z=[001].

Proximity histogram: Composition/at.% (0–20) vs Distance/nm (−5 to ~1.5), same eight-element legend, arrows marking Matrix (left) and Clusters (NiAl) (right). Ni and Al rise to ~9 and ~8 at.% toward the cluster centre; Si, Mo and Cr increase at the right edge; C decreases to ~0; error bars shown.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an APT reconstruction with brown isoconcentration surfaces forming needle-like/plate-like precipitates arranged in rows within the matrix; a 20 nm scale bar is printed.

Panel (d) shows green isoconcentration surfaces as a much denser population of small near-spherical clusters than the brown features in (a), and a printed colour key labels green = NiAl and brown = ε-carbide.

Panel (b) is an HRTEM image with a 2 nm scale bar, a cyan boxed region labelled 'ε-carbide', a matrix labelled 'Bcc', and an FFT inset whose spots are labelled (020)Ni and (002)ε with zone axes Z=[100]Ni and Z=[110]ε.
Panel (e) is an HRTEM image with a 2 nm scale bar, a green boxed region labelled 'B2-NiAl' in a 'Bcc' matrix, and an FFT inset labelled (200)Ni and (100)NiAl with Z=[001].

In panel (c) the C profile rises from roughly 1.5 at.% in the matrix to about 8.5–9 at.% inside the ε-carbide region, while the Ni curve stays near 5.5 at.%, Si near 4 at.% and Al between ~2.5 and ~4 at.%.

In panel (f) the Ni and Al profiles rise toward the NiAl cluster centre (approximately 9 at.% Ni and 8 at.% Al near the right edge) while the C profile falls toward ~0, and Si, Mo and Cr show enrichment at the right edge.
Both proximity histograms are plotted with Composition in at.% (axis 0–20) against Distance in nm (axis from −5 to about +1.5) and show error bars on the data.

The caption states that (a) and (d) are 5 at.% C and 10 at.% Ni + Al isoconcentration surfaces showing ε-carbides and NiAl clusters, (b) and (e) are TEM images with FFT patterns, and (c) and (f) are proximity histograms, all obtained from the 1.3Al steel.
The caption states that slight Ni and Al enrichment is detected at the centres of the ε-carbides, which contrasts with the flat Ni and Al profiles visible in (c) over the plotted −5 to ~1.5 nm range.
The citing text states that needle-like C-rich precipitates have an average thickness of ~2.2 nm and a spacing of ~10 nm and are uniformly distributed in the matrix (Fig. 5(a)).
The citing text states that TEM and FFT analysis confirm the C-rich precipitates are hcp-structured ε-carbides viewed along the [110] zone axis (Fig. 5(b)).

The citing text states that NiAl clusters have a number density of 4.88 × 10^24 m^-3 and an equivalent radius of 0.57 nm, and that the FFT in Fig. 5(e) shows a bcc structure along the [001] zone axis with a fully coherent NiAl/matrix interface.

The citing text states that the atomic concentrations of Ni and Al at the cluster centres are approximately 13 at.%, lower than the stoichiometric NiAl composition, indicating early-stage nucleation; the plotted Ni and Al values in (f) appear lower (~9 and ~8 at.%), so the image value and the citation value are not identical.

The citing text states that the central region of the ε-carbides reaches a carbon concentration as high as 8.91 at.% with Ni ~5.50 at.% and Al ~2.60 at.%, and that the region surrounding the NiAl clusters maintains a carbon concentration of ~1.0 at.%.
The citing text states that ε-carbides and NiAl clusters nucleate and grow independently during tempering, with no elemental overlap or competitive partitioning between C and Ni/Al.

unreadable_items: Panels (c) and (f): the right-hand end of the curves is truncated by the plot edge, so the final data points just beyond the last x-tick (~1.5 nm) cannot be read precisely
Panels (c) and (f): individual error-bar magnitudes are not quantifiable from the rendered resolution
